newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares close firm, focus on new issues.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares close firm, focus on new issues.

text.p: Singapore shares closed firmer though off their highs on Tuesday with much of the activity centred on recently listed issues.
"Most of the IPO shares are up today, especially those in the electronics sector," said one dealer.
Component disk maker MMI Holdings topped the actives with over 14 million shares. The shares rose over 11 percent to end at S$0.73 (US$0.50). A dealer said fair value for MMI was at S$0.78.
Other active new issues included Gul Technologies and Serial System, both of which closed higher at S$0.705 and S$0.635, respectively.

The wider market also saw buying in bank and property stocks despite the uncertain outlook in property prices. The SES property index ended 16.41 points higher at 687.21 led by gains in City Developments and Keppel Land.
"The market has been oversold and investors are just looking for something to buy," said one dealer.

The Straits Times Industrial index closed 27.08 points higher at 2,055.68. Market volume was a brisk 187.6 millin shares with 276 gainers against 113 losers. Gainers included Wing Tai, Creative and Singapore Press foreign while Keppel Corp and Singapore Telecom ended lower.
